title: Adaptive table density and intuitive column resize behaviors
creator: Lena Park
description:
Problem: Our Table component currently exposes multiple density options and a column resize affordance that behaves inconsistently across screens and when virtualization is enabled. Teams building admin UIs and analytics dashboards report awkward column resizing (jumpy header, misaligned cell content) and unclear defaults for density, which leads to duplicated work and visual regressions across products.

Goal: Define a cohesive set of density tokens and an accessible, predictable column-resize interaction that works with virtualized rendering and preserves keyboard/assistive patterns. Deliver updated design specs, token usage guidance, Figma components, and a migration checklist for engineers + a small experiment to evaluate default density selection for dashboards.

Scope: Visual density tokens (rowHeight, verticalPadding, font-size adjustments), three density modes (Comfortable, Compact, Dense), column resize UX (drag, double-click auto-fit, snap increments), keyboard controls for resizing, virtualization edge cases (preserve resize state as columns rerender), and updated docs with code snippets and a migration guide.
acceptance_criteria: Design tokens for table densities defined and documented (rowHeight, padding, token names) with values for desktop and tablet
Figma component variants for Table with three density modes and responsive previews
High-fidelity interaction specs for column resizing: drag behavior, double-click auto-fit, keyboard resize with arrow keys and modifier, and visual feedback states
Edge-case flows documented for virtualization (sticky headers, preserved column widths after data refresh/scroll, and no layout jumps)
Accessibility checklist satisfied: screen-reader announcements for column resize start/stop, focus order preserved, and contrast of resize handles meets AA
Design system docs updated with migration steps and recommended defaults; engineering has a clear API proposal for props and events
tasks: Audit current Table component usages across Console and internal apps to collect density defaults (ENG/PM pairing)
Define canonical token names and numeric values for desktop/tablet for Comfortable / Compact / Dense
Produce Figma component set with interactive prototyping (drag and double-click emulation)
Write interaction spec for engineers including animation timings, snap increments, min/max widths, and overflow behavior
Coordinate with Eng on virtualization behavior: preserve resize state in column metadata and reapply on row buffer changes
Draft docs + migration checklist and example code for both legacy Table props and new unified API (prop names + events)
Run quick usability test (5 product engineers/designers) to validate discoverability of resize affordance and density selector
design_notes: Prefer token-driven approach so density can be toggled globally or per-table; tokens should map to semantic names: table.row-height.[comfortable|compact|dense], table.cell-vertical-padding.[comfortable|compact|dense]

Resize interaction: pointer drag updates a live preview of column width; show thin overlay guide while dragging to avoid reflowing all cells during drag (minimize layout thrashing when virtualization enabled)

Double-click on resize handle should auto-fit to longest visible cell content (not entire dataset) to avoid expensive measurements with virtualization; provide API to trigger full-auto-fit if consumer opts in
Keyboard accessibility: when resize handle is focused, left/right arrows adjust width by 4px, Shift+arrow adjusts by 16px; Enter/Space begins and ends a drag-like resize mode for SR users
When virtualization causes cell content to mount/unmount, column width must be stored in column state (not ephemeral DOM width) so resizing persists across buffer shifts
Consider default density: run opt-in experiment where dashboards default to Compact and admin tables default to Comfortable; use telemetry to evaluate density switch rates
